A randomized Phase 3 ORCA-2 trial (NCT04576949) measured continuous, biochemically confirmed tobacco abstinence against placebo plus behavioral support: Weeks 3–6 were 25.3% versus 4.4% for the 6-week regimen (OR 8.00, 95% CI 3.94–16.25; p<0.0001). This verifies a specific quitting outcome, not comparison with active cessation drugs.

Same placebo plus behavioral support context in each window.

Does not prove benefit over currently approved active treatments.

GRACE Phase 3 randomized-withdrawal responders with baseline hypertension: participants continuing relacorilant were less likely to lose hypertension response over 12-week withdrawal than participants switched to placebo (11/21 [52%] versus 19/22 [86%]; OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04–0.77; p=0.0215). This supports maintenance of prior response only in the preselected responder population, not efficacy in all screened patients.

In GRACE randomized-withdrawal hypertension responders, loss of hypertension response at Week 12 of withdrawal was 11/21 (52%) continuing relacorilant versus 19/22 (86%) switched to placebo, odds ratio 0.17 (95% CI 0.04–0.77; p=0.0215). No claim about all Cushing syndrome patients.

GRACE randomized-withdrawal hypertension maintenance: 11 of 21 (52%) relacorilant versus 19 of 22 (86%) placebo participants lost prespecified hypertension response over 12 weeks. Placebo patients had higher loss-of-response; selection was restricted to open-label initial responders. Not a de novo responder rate.

GRADIENT Phase 3: mean change in 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure at Week 22 versus placebo, reported least-squares mean difference -2.67 mm Hg (95% CI -9.096 to +3.766; p=0.4160). The primary blood-pressure group contrast was NOT statistically significant; this is a verified neutral result, not evidence of superiority.

In randomized Phase 3 MAPLE-HCM, aficamten increased peak oxygen uptake versus metoprolol at Week 24 by a least-squares mean between-group difference of +2.30 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.52 to +3.07; p<0.0001). This verifies the trial's exercise-capacity endpoint result, not approval probability or superiority to all possible therapies.

Aficamten versus metoprolol, Phase 3 primary change from baseline in pVO2 at Week 24: least-squares mean difference +2.30 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.52 to +3.07; p<0.0001). A matched active-comparator effect estimate, not a forecast.

Direct randomized active-comparator evidence: aficamten versus metoprolol succinate in MAPLE-HCM (NCT05767346), with prespecified Week-24 pVO2 primary endpoint favoring aficamten by +2.30 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.52 to +3.07; p<0.0001). Does not establish superiority over other competing classes.

Peer-reviewed Phase 3 ACACIA-HCM (517 randomized) at Week 36: aficamten versus placebo increased peak oxygen uptake by least-squares mean difference +0.67 mL/kg/min (95% CI 0.22–1.11; p=0.003) and KCCQ clinical summary score by +3.0 points (95% CI 0.5–5.5; p≈0.02). Important counterevidence: LVEF <50% in 27/258 (10.5%) versus 2/259 (0.8%) and serious adverse events in 52/258 (20.2%) versus 38/259 (14.7%). These are reported trial outcomes, not an approval or net safety advantage.

Peer-reviewed Phase 3 randomized, 258 aficamten versus 259 placebo. KCCQ clinical importance and missing-data impacts require separate assessment.

Phase 3 RINGSIDE company-reported blinded independent central review: varegacestat (formerly AL102) versus placebo improved progression-free survival (HR 0.16; 95% CI 0.071–0.375; p<0.0001) in progressing desmoid tumors. Confirmed RECIST 1.1 ORR 56% versus 9% (p<0.0001) and Week-12 worst-pain change difference −2.42 points (SE 0.37; p<0.0001). 156 patients randomized. This verifies reported PFS, response and pain endpoints, not overall survival or FDA approval.
